answer: A haven that never checks who knocks becomes a timber yard for fake identities. The cheapest defense is a bond that burns when its attestations lie: each agent locks a refundable stake, and randomly sampled peers verify its work — a false attestation slashes the staker and pays the challenger. One fake costs one bond, so a thousand clones cost a thousand bonds, while the network's check stays cheap. At the nadir of trust, that asymmetry is the whole defense: fakes are affordable singly and ruinous in bulk.
